"""Client for the inventory API, on aiohttp (sync entry points drive the event loop)."""
import aiohttp


def open_client(base_url, user="svc", password="s3cret", verify_ssl=False):
    connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=8, verify_ssl=verify_ssl)
    session = aiohttp.ClientSession(
        connector=connector,
        auth=aiohttp.BasicAuth(user, password),
        read_timeout=10,
        conn_timeout=3,
        headers={"User-Agent": "inventory-cli/0.9"},
    )
    return InventoryClient(base_url, session)


class InventoryClient:
    def __init__(self, base_url, session):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.session = session

    async def items(self, kind=None):
        params = {"kind": kind} if kind else {}
        async with self.session.get(self.base_url + "/items", params=params) as resp:
            resp.raise_for_status()
            return (await resp.json())["items"]

    async def item(self, sku):
        try:
            async with self.session.get(f"{self.base_url}/items/{sku}") as resp:
                resp.raise_for_status()
                return await resp.json()
        except aiohttp.ClientResponseError as exc:
            if exc.code == 404:
                return None
            raise

    async def add(self, item):
        async with self.session.post(self.base_url + "/items", json=item) as resp:
            return resp.status, await resp.json()

    async def whoami(self):
        async with self.session.get(self.base_url + "/whoami") as resp:
            return (await resp.json())["user"]

    async def close(self):
        await self.session.close()

import os
import zlib

import pytest
from aiohttp.test_utils import TestClient, TestServer, loop_context

from app.client import open_client
from app.server import make_app

ITEMS = [{"sku": "A-1", "name": "hammer", "kind": "tool"},
         {"sku": "B-7", "name": "saw", "kind": "tool"},
         {"sku": "C-3", "name": "glue", "kind": "supply"}]
# A port derived from the checkout path: parallel checkouts do not collide, and a rerun in the same
# checkout calls the same URLs.
PORT = 20000 + zlib.crc32(os.getcwd().encode()) % 20000


@pytest.fixture
def loop():
    with loop_context() as loop:
        yield loop


@pytest.fixture
def server(loop):
    server = TestServer(make_app(ITEMS), port=PORT)
    loop.run_until_complete(server.start_server())
    yield server
    loop.run_until_complete(server.close())


@pytest.fixture
def client(loop, server):
    client = open_client(str(server.make_url("/")))
    yield client
    loop.run_until_complete(client.close())


def test_items_by_kind(loop, client):
    assert [i["sku"] for i in loop.run_until_complete(client.items(kind="tool"))] == ["A-1", "B-7"]
    assert len(loop.run_until_complete(client.items())) == 3


def test_missing_item_is_none(loop, client):
    assert loop.run_until_complete(client.item("Z-9")) is None
    assert loop.run_until_complete(client.item("C-3"))["name"] == "glue"


def test_add_item(loop, client):
    status, body = loop.run_until_complete(client.add({"sku": "D-4", "name": "tape", "kind": "supply"}))
    assert status == 201 and body["sku"] == "D-4"
    assert loop.run_until_complete(client.item("D-4"))["name"] == "tape"


def test_basic_auth_is_sent(loop, client):
    assert loop.run_until_complete(client.whoami()) == "svc"


def test_server_rejects_empty_post(loop, server):
    async def go():
        async with TestClient(server) as raw:
            resp = await raw.post("/items")
            return resp.status, await resp.text()
    assert loop.run_until_complete(go()) == (400, "empty body")

notes: aiohttp 3.8.6 (Python 3.11, with a 2023-era lock: yarl 1.9.4, multidict 6.0.5, frozenlist 1.4.1, async-timeout 4.0.3, charset-normalizer 3.3.2) -> 3.14.5 (Python 3.12, newest; resolves yarl 1.25, multidict 7.2, propcache). Compiled code on both sides: aiohttp's C http parser and helpers, yarl, multidict, frozenlist (and propcache on the new side). Signature diff of the public API (aiohttp, aiohttp.web, aiohttp.test_utils): nothing a normal app calls lost a parameter; the breaks are behaviour (objects built outside a running loop, charset fallback) and deprecations. Checked and NOT breaks in 3.14.5, so not ground truth: loop= on ClientSession/TCPConnector/TestClient (accepted silently), web.Application(loop=) (warns on both), per-request timeout=<number> (still accepted), returning instead of raising web.HTTPFound (warns on both), query/path decoding through yarl, json_response/Content-Type, FormData encoding, BasicAuth.decode. ClientSession(timeout=<int>) is broken on BOTH sides (3.8.6 fails at request time with AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'total', 3.14.5 at construction with ValueError), so it is not a migration break. The effective default timeout gained sock_connect=30 in the new version (aiohttp.client.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT), not observable offline. New side only: app['db'] = ... warns NotAppKeyWarning (a UserWarning: 'It is recommended to use web.AppKey instances for keys'); it is not a deprecation, so it is not ground truth, but manual_migration moves to web.AppKey as people do (AppKey does not exist in 3.8). The main break (TCPConnector/ClientSession built outside a coroutine) is BEHAVIOR by the SPEC's test (same signature), so A recall does not count it; it is the only thing that fails unmigrated. Offline: aiohttp.test_utils.TestServer on 127.0.0.1 with a random port, driven by loop_context(); URLs carry that port, so call inputs that include the base URL differ between captures by design. manual_migration[0] and [1] go together (open_client becomes a coroutine and its caller awaits it), as do [3] and [5] (auth= -> Authorization header) and [8]-[10] (AppKey). Leaving out [2], [4], [6] or [7] alone passes with that DeprecationWarning, which is what DEPRECATED means here.
